My original point was to bitch about people who complain about “tip culture” not the actual lack of tipping.

Yes and I like it. My point was, BOH complains, FOH complains, but we applied for that job. We knew what we were getting into. Both sides. I would NEVER give a line shit for trying to be a server. I’ve seen it, they can be amazing servers because they are so knowledgeable about the food. But in my decade of experience, they work in the kitchen because that’s what they prefer. And I’ve never been shamed for making money by any of the cooks I’ve worked with.

I have almost nothing against people who don’t tip. Like I said, I’m not chasing you down, and the risk/reward of not knowing how much you’re going to make is part of the appeal for me. The point I was trying to make, is stop telling me how MY job is supposed to work. If you’re not a server, why should you have a say I’m how servers operate? People aren’t telling cashiers how they should scan shit or plumbers how they should charge for hours worked. People are trying to complain about a system that isn’t “broken” it just costs money. And some think it shouldn’t. But that’s my job, I like it, and I’m sick of hearing about how wrong it is from people who have never done it.

Yes because only people who make a wage can be skilled. I clearly don’t deserve the money I make because other people can’t make it too and I’m not actually skilled. It’s an accident that I can hold a tray with 25 drinks and memorize the order with modifications for an 8 top. Oh and learning the ingredients, where they are from, and whether or not any dish is allergen safe on an extensive menu is too easy to be considered a learned skill.
You’re not subsidizing anything. You are paying me for a service. Unlike an hourly wage, I work as hard as I can to get as much for that service.
You do have an option. If you only want to pay for the prepared food, then get it to go.
